title: Hidden Gauge Freedom in Complex-Pole Hierarchical Equations of Motion
abstract: While complex-pole hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) have dramatically expanded the reach of numerically exact quantum dynamics simulations of open quantum systems, they suffer from numerical instabilities rooted in the non-Hermitian structure of their Liouvillian. Yet, the origin of this structure remains obscure. Here, we report a previously unknown gauge freedom in complex-pole HEOM: a continuous family of analytically equivalent Liouvillians, all encoding the same bath correlation function, whose numerical properties vary dramatically. This gauge controls both the eigenspectrum and non-normality of the hierarchy generator, revealing spectral divergence and non-normal error amplification as two distinct instability mechanisms. By optimizing this gauge, we introduce GO--HEOM, which eliminates divergences in strongly coupled Brownian oscillator environments and extends numerically exact simulations of sub-Ohmic dynamics -- including through the delocalized-to-localized quantum phase transition -- to previously inaccessible coupling strengths. Because this gauge transformation is independent of the bath-correlation decomposition scheme, our GO--HEOM becomes a general, broadly compatible strategy for accessing numerically exact quantum dynamics of open quantum systems over arbitrary coupling and highly non-Markovian regimes.
summary: The paper reveals a hidden gauge freedom within the complex-pole HEOM used for open quantum systems. By optimizing this gauge parameter, they introduce GO-HEOM, a numerically stable variant of the simulation technique. This advancement allows researchers to accurately model dynamics in strongly coupled or highly non-Markovian environments previously unreachable by standard methods.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the numerical instability inherent in complex-pole Hierarchical Equations of Motion (HEOM) when simulating open quantum systems.
main_result: The authors discovered a continuous, previously unknown gauge freedom within the HEOM formulation, allowing for the development of GO-HEOM which stabilizes simulations in strongly coupled and highly non-Markovian regimes.
method: They derive this gauge freedom by reformulating the Liouvillian structure and optimizing a gauge parameter ($\phi$) to minimize numerical artifacts like spectral divergence and non-normal error amplification.
model_or_system: The work focuses on open quantum systems, using the spin-boson model as a primary benchmark. The dynamics are governed by the HEOM derived from the bath correlation function.
key_observables: Population difference $\langle\sigma_z(t)angle$, non-normality ($\eta_H$), and the eigenvalue spectrum of the hierarchy generator.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($p_0$ or $\alpha$), spectral density type (e.g., sub-Ohmic $\alpha=0.2$ to $0.02$), and the gauge parameter ($\phi_r$).
main_assumptions: The gauge transformation is shown to be independent of the specific bath-correlation decomposition scheme, suggesting general applicability.
figures_summary: Figures compare dynamics ($\langle\sigma_z(t)angle$) across different gauge parameters ($\phi_r$), demonstrating that GO-HEOM stabilizes simulations where conventional HEOM diverges. Other figures illustrate spectral analysis and convergence checks.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the instability in standard complex-pole HEOM, then derives the continuous gauge freedom ($\phi$). It introduces GO-HEOM by optimizing $\phi$ to stabilize dynamics, demonstrating its success across various coupling regimes and finally relating the method to a generalized Quantum Fokker-Planck Equation.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general methodological tool (GO-HEOM) for simulating complex open quantum dynamics that was previously computationally inaccessible due to numerical instability, directly impacting research in quantum optics and molecular physics.
